test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The percentage profit earned by selling an article for ₹6,833 is equal to the percentage loss incurred by selling the same article for ₹1,447. At what price should the article be sold (in ₹) to make a 45% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **Profit% = Loss%** for two selling prices, the **Cost Price (CP)** is the average of those two prices.

CP = (6833 + 1447) ÷ 2 = 8280 ÷ 2 = 4140.

To make a **45% profit**, required SP = CP × 1.45.

SP = 4140 × 145 ÷ 100 = 41.4 × 145 = 6003.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,003.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP₁ = ₹6,833, SP₂ = ₹1,447, Profit% = Loss%, Desired Profit% = 45%.

**Formulas:** CP = (SP₁ + SP₂) ÷ 2 (if Profit% = Loss%), SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/336f369ce82e3cc41ef5f72220d2f3a1e8d2e3b82ebae86fcb84ff53bbb06475.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price** be x.

⇒ Profit% = [(6833 − x) ÷ x] × 100 and Loss% = [(x − 1447) ÷ x] × 100.

⇒ 6833 − x = x − 1447 ⇒ 2x = 8280 ⇒ x = **4140**.

⇒ New Selling Price = 4140 × (100 + 45) ÷ 100 = 4140 × 1.45.

⇒ New SP = **6003**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,003.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price when Profit = Loss

When numerical profit equals numerical loss for two different selling prices, the CP is always the arithmetic mean of those prices: CP = (SPₕᵢgₕ + SPₗₒw) ÷ 2.

Calculating Profit Selling Price

To calculate a specific profit percentage P%, use the multiplier: SP = CP × (1 + P ÷ 100).
